newsitem.title: COLUMBIA: 12 bodies found after rebel clash in east Colombia.
newsitem.headline: 12 bodies found after rebel clash in east Colombia.

text.p: At least 12 bodies clothed in military-style uniforms -- suspected victims of a clash with leftist rebels -- were found near a remote town in eastern Colombia, the Chief Prosecutor's office said on Thursday.

The bodies were discovered on Wednesday near Mapiripan in Meta province a week after the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) said it had killed 26 soldiers posing as right-wing paramilitary fighters.
A spokesman at the prosecutor's office was unable to confirm the identity of the dead and said he did not know where the corpses had been taken.
"We found 12 bodies. There have been very serious clashes in this zone and people no longer dare go and bury their dead," the spokesman said.
In two separate incidents in northern Sucre province Thursday, three peasants and a municipal councilor were shot to death by suspected paramilitary fighters, police said.
Mapiripan municipal government secretary Jorge Duque said by telephone that investigators told him some of the 12 found dead nearby had been wearing combat fatigues.

All the bodies were found in La Cooperativa, a hamlet about 25 miles (40 km) from Mapiripan -- where about 30 peasants, many of them members of the Communist Party and suspected leftist sympathizers, were massacred in July.
Political analysts say Colombia's eastern plains region is emerging as one of the new flashpoints in the country's long- running internal war.

In a communique issued last Friday, the FARC said those killed in La Cooperativa on Aug. 2 were soldiers who took part in the Mapiripan massacre. The Colombian police initially said a hitherto unknown right-wing paramilitary group was responsible for the murders.
